headline: A 600-year-old book that no one on Earth can read.
slides: About 240 pages of unknown writing, strange plants, star charts and bathing figures.
Book dealer Wilfrid Voynich bought it. It's been at Yale since 1969.
In 2009 the parchment was radiocarbon-dated to 1404-1438.
Top WWI and WWII cryptographers, including William Friedman, tried and failed.
Dozens of people have announced solutions. None has held up.
The whole thing is free online at Yale's Beinecke Library. Have a go.
sources: Sources: Beinecke Rare Book & Manuscript Library (MS 408), University of Arizona radiocarbon study (2011)
